pressure, led 6 it switched off and led 7 is switched on. At the third pressure of the button,

- Call the insertionSort subroutine, passing the address of the array of char and the 
number of initialized elements. The subroutine will sort the elements of the array, 
considering them as signed byte values. 
- When the subroutine ends, switch on led 11.

Question 2 (6 points) 
Extend the project to control leds 8-11 based on the values generated by the LCG. 
First, start timer 0 in order to generate an interrupt every 3 seconds. 
Then, in the handler of timer 0, call the nextElementLCG subroutine to obtain the n-th element 
of the sequence. Since the value ranges in [0, 254], compute the modulo 4 of such value: 
- if value mod 4 == 0, switch on led 11 
- if value mod 4 == 1, switch on led 10 
- if value mod 4 == 2, switch on led 9 
- if value mod 4 == 3, switch on led 8 
Use the same parameters as in the example: seed 1, a = 131, c = 7, n = index of the loop, m = 255. 
The nextElementLCG subroutine is called only 10 times (i.e., during the first 10 interrupts of 
timer 0). The leds are switched on in the following order:

A2 
iteration n Xn Xn mod 4 Led on 
0 138 2 9 
1 234 2 9 
 
Important: Ensure that only one led is on at any given time. Before switching on a new led, turn off 
the previously lit led (from the previous timer interrupt). 
 
 
Question 3 (6 points) 
Extend the project to implement a rhythm game using the joystick on the board. The game will 
involve moving the joystick in response to the leds being switched on. 
When a led lights up, the player must move the joystick accordingly: 
- led 11: move the joystick up 
- led 10: move the joystick left 
- led 9: move the joystick right 
- led 8: move the joystick down 
Only the first movement of the joystick has to be considered (further movements within the 3-
second interval are ignored). If the movement corresponds to the correct direction for the lit led, 
increment the variable num_correct, otherwise increment num_wrong. Regardless of the 
correctness, after the joystick movement the led is immediately switched off. 
The game continues for 10 sequence elements. After 10 elements, the game ends and the player's 
score is evaluated. If num_correct > num_wrong, the player wins: turn on led 4 to indicate 
victory. Otherwise, the player looses: turn on led 5 to indicate defeat.

In this part, you implement a game of bulls and cows with the LPC1768 board. 
In the main function, start a timer of your choice. 
 
The player presses the joystick (i.e., select function) to start the game. In this first moment: 
- all LEDs are turned off 
- the player’s guess is initialized to 0000 
- the timer counter is used to generate the secret code. 
In detail, the secret code is generated from the four least significant hexadecimal digits of the timer 
counter. Each hexadecimal digit is masked with 0x3 in order to obtain a value in the range [0-3]. 
Example: timerCounter = 0x00121AB6 
 
The player moves the joystick to choose the four digits of their guess: 
- when the joystick moves down, the first digit of the guess is incremented. If the value 
becomes 4, then it is reset to 0. The binary representation of guess[0] is displayed on LEDs 
10 and 11. For example, if guess[0] = 2, then LED 10 is turned on and LED 11 is turned off. 
- when the joystick moves left, the second digit of the guess is incremented. If the value 
becomes 4, then it is reset to 0. The binary representation of guess[1] is displayed on LEDs 
8 and 9. 
- when the joystick moves right, the third digit of the guess is incremented. If the value 
becomes 4, then it is reset to 0. The binary representation of guess[2] is displayed on LEDs 
6 and 7. 
- when the joystick moves up, the fourth digit of the guess is incremented. If the value 
becomes 4, then it is reset to 0. The binary representation of guess[3] is displayed on LEDs 
4 and 5. 
 
When the player is satisfied with their guess, they press the joystick. The BullsAndCows 
subroutine is then called passing guess, secret and two arrays initialized to zero. The value returned 
by the subroutine is shown on the LEDs, assuming LED4 represents the most significant digit and 
LED 11 the least significant one. 
 
The player can press the joystick again to compose another guess. At this moment: 
- all LEDs are turned off 
- the player’s guess is initialized to 0000 
Note that the secret code must not be changed. 
 
Then, the game continues alternating between joystick movements to set the guess and subroutine 
calls to compute the number of bulls and cows. The game ends when the number of bulls is 4, i.e., 
LEDs 4-7 are turned on and LEDs 8-11 are turned off. No specific action is required when the game 
ends.
